Static on the Wire

The telegraph in the corner had not spoken in eleven years, but at noon it clicked twice and was quiet again.

Bruno crossed the room and lifted the brass cover with the care of a man opening a letter not addressed to him.

“Dust does not make a relay click,” Bruno said. “Something is on the wire.”

Alice brought the log book to the window, where the light was good enough to read by.

“The line was cut below the trestle in the flood year,” Alice said. “I filed that report myself.”

A moth settled on the key, and neither of them brushed it away.

“Then the wire has a long memory,” Bruno said, and he wrote the time down anyway.

They listened until the kettle boiled over, and the sound of the water on the stove was almost a relief.

“If it clicks again, we answer it,” Alice said, and the station settled back into the wind.
